Dundee manager Steven Pressley is nothing if not honest. Having taken full responsibility for his team’s 8-0 thrashing by Hearts on Saturday, he now admits that the experience left him wanting to ‘crawl under a rock and hide’.

You won’t hear him writing it off as a ‘bad day at the office’ or branding it a freak result from which he and his players would quickly move on. Dundee’s heaviest-ever home defeat in the league was an indignity that really hit their popular manager. And hit him hard.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s been a difficult 24-48 hours,’ noted Pressley. ‘There’s been a lot of hurt, a lot of embarrassment. As you can imagine, at times I’ve wanted to crawl under a rock and hide.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s difficult on the back of such a disappointing result. But I will say this: I suffer a lot from vulnerability at times, but for some reason during difficult moments I seem to find strength from somewhere.

‘I don’t know if it’s from my family, from messages that I’ve received, from my reading. But I’ve had to show strength. I have to support the players. I have to make sure we navigate our way out of what was a really embarrassing moment.

‘We had a good meeting yesterday. We chatted a lot about the various aspects, and hopefully we can start responding to the disappointment.’.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley states he felt hurt and embarrassed after losing 8-0 to Hearts.

Defender Ryan Astley struggles to take in Dundee's heaviest-ever home defeat in the league.

That process starts tomorrow night against Hibs, who suffered a humiliation of their own when they lost 4-0 at home to Dundee United on Saturday. Pressley says the immediate objective for his team is to go there with a better attitude than they have shown lately.

He had feared a setback coming for Dundee – ‘not 8-0 but a disappointing performance’ – because he had ‘sensed a little bit of subconscious complacency’. He felt his team had been over-hyped by outsiders on the back of a start to the season in which they won five of their 12 matches before the international break.

It has been revealed that ‘We’re nowhere near the levels that people keep telling us we are,’ he said. ‘We’re not a good enough team not to do the hard yards. Our whole strength has been built on the cohesion of the team, the unity of the team, the aggressiveness of the team.

Industry observers note that ‘And I think what Saturday did highlight is exactly what I’ve been saying. If we get lazy on the hard yards, we’re a very vulnerable team. We have to be at our absolute best to get results.’.

He hopes the Hearts game will be ‘a reset moment’ that eventually helps his players to improve, but there are no guarantees from Pressley that they will shake it off at Easter Road tomorrow.

According to recent reports, asked if he expected a positive response from them, he noted: ‘I don’t know. I know that they’re hurting. I know that they want to respond in the best possible way. That part I don’t question. I know how much it’s affected them.

It has been revealed that ‘But we’ve not had a lot of time. I just hope we can bring some pride back to the football club with the right type of performance.’.

Industry observers note that the good news for Dundee is that they are up against a team who have been hopeless in their own stadium recently. Second-bottom Hibs have lost nine of their last ten Premiership games at Easter Road and haven’t taken three points there since early April.

Supporters turned on the Edinburgh side after the defeat by Dundee United, but Hibs midfielder Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea that he and his team-mates don’t enjoy playing in their own ground.

Jamie McGrath was in the Hibs side that suffered another defeat at Easter Road on Saturday.

In a recent development, ‘Personally, I always like playing at home,’ stated McGrath. ‘I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a substantial open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb.’.

It looked like Marink Reedijk’s side had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

In a recent development, so McGrath is hoping Saturday’s aberration was a blip. ‘We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us. We were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams. It’s frustrating not to build on that.’.

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs’ lowly league position and senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

‘It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute. It’s obviously not where we want to be. We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.’.

One of the most uplifting facets of Martin Drury's full-time tenure has been the transformation so far in 2026-27.

A good barometer of their improvement arrives in tonight's Yorkshire derby at Doncaster Rovers - on an evening when three points would see the Terriers move level on points with leaders Stockport County.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A poor night at the South Yorkshire venue in February saw Town lose 1-0 in a toothless and tepid showing which received jeers from travelling fans at half-time and the final whistle.

In a recent development, it was one a number of bad days on the road. Others were played out at Oakwell, Valley Parade and further afield at Adams Park and Home Park.

There were plenty more too, especially in the second half of the season when the entertainment value was lamentably low.

In the away table in 25-26, Huddersfield were ranked a below-par 13th, with 25 points from 23 games. Refreshingly, the picture is changing, not just in terms of points ratio, but goals and chance creation.

Town have averaged two points a game on the road so far, with 14 points from their seven matches. It's currently the second best record in the division, factoring in goal difference.

Drury observed: "There was some criticism of the away form last season. Obviously, I came in February. Between February and the end of the season, the away form wasn't brilliant.

It has been revealed that "Prior to that, for the seven months before that, there weren't enough points picked up on the road. And if you want to be successful, you need to do that.

"So that was certainly an area that we addressed in the summer. And we did some things around that with the players, both on and off the grass, around certain scenarios and places that you're going to go to and how we might play when we're home and away. I think the players have been brilliant.

"I think we're fourth or third best in the league, maybe, for away form at the current time.

Recent findings suggest that "We're going to lose some games away. That's going to happen. But I have to say, the things that we wanted to try and learn from last season and get better at, the players have done really, really well with that.

"And we've gone to some tough places so far with different types of challenges that we've enjoyed and embraced.".

Town face a Rovers side who don't usually mind derbies. They excelled, certainly in the first half, of the home game with Sheffield Wednesday last month and revealed character to come from behind to secure a hard-earned stoppage-time point at Bradford City on Saturday.

The latter derby marked the first-team return of ex-Terriers defender Matty Pearson after almost two-and-a-half months out with injury.

Pearson came through the weekend draw, while Jamie Sterry, James Husband and Tommi O’Reilly are all in contention for tonight's game.

Industry observers note that eager to make up for lost time, Pearson commented: "It's one of those things, you feel helpless when you're injured. It's been a tough few months but I'm well past that now.

"It's how you handle things and react. I think everyone's career has ups and downs and it's how you bounce back and how you react to them situations.".

Pearson unquestionably had a mixed time during his four seasons at Huddersfield.

The Keighley-born player continued: "It was a massive change really. We had an unbelievable first season (2021-22) and got into the play-offs and final (against Nottingham Forest at Wembley).

Recent findings suggest that "And then it was 'sliding doors'. I don't know the full ins and outs but we struggled for the following two or three seasons after that. We went from playoffs to relegation battles every season.

"It's hard to say exactly what went on, it's one of those where it's been taken over now and they look like they're having a good season so far.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

It has been revealed that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

In a recent development, but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

Recent findings suggest that for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

In a recent development, the Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews stated. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

It has been revealed that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Industry observers note that any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very crucial points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

In a recent development, an encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their massive-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca mentioned in his pre-match press conference.”.

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”.

Ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

In a recent development, elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Recent findings suggest that breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be remarked for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

Pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

The Polish side ground out a hard-fought 1-1 draw against Sunderland, but Benfica proved too strong in their next outing, handing them a 3-1 defeat on matchday four.

Having scored just two goals and conceded 12, they are among the three teams languishing near the bottom of the table with only one point, with only FC Ararat-Armenia faring worse.

Rovers find themselves in the final relegation spot ahead of Thursday night's televised home derby with second-placed Huddersfield Town.

McCann's side have won just once in their past six league outings, losing four - although the sole victory arrived against Yorkshire opposition, a 2-0 home success over Sheffield Wednesday on October 24.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A gutsy late derby point at Bradford City, last time out, was also welcome, even if McCann has not been spared criticism from supporters in recent times, particularly following atrocious losses at MK Dons and Kidderminster Harriers.

Sharp, 40, who left Rovers at the end of last season - hitting a hat-trick in his final game in May—mentioned: "I think Grant's showed his pedigree with two promotions from League Two and League One.

"He'll be chomping at the bit trying to get up the table because he's an ambitious manager who wants promotion, which is no different to what I would be.

"I think it's tough because he believes a lot in the players and I think it needs to rub off on the players.

Recent findings suggest that "He always used to say it to me and the group: 'don't let me believe in you as much as you believe in each other'. And I think that may be the difference at the minute.

Sources indicate that "I think some of the players need to step up a little bit more. I'm not going to name names, but they'll know who they are. They've got to all start pulling in the right direction and getting that club moving up the table.".

Despite a difficult season so far for Rovers, boardroom support for McCann appears solid and unwavering - with the Northern Irishman having a strong working relationship with owner Terry Bramall and chief executive officer Gavin Baldwin.

Industry observers note that sharp, at Doncaster Sports College earlier this week as part of the EFL's Power of 72 campaign that celebrates the work that clubs and their charities do in the local community, continued: "I think (most) managers are three losses away from being under pressure. I think that's how it is in this day and age; you don't get the time.

In a recent development, "Managers are always asking for time. But I think if you don't win games, you're always under pressure as the media are on your back and fans.

Recent findings suggest that "Ultimately, if that's happening, some of the players might turn on you. So the most crucial thing is the players and keeping them happy, especially the ones who aren't in the team, because you always need them throughout the season.

"Having as much good noise as you can have in your dressing room and your club fends off the media and all the negative noise surrounding it.

"If you can keep it out when it isn't going great - it’s probably not going as great as Grant and Doncaster would like at the minute - (that's good).

"But I know that he's got full backing of the board and the players. It's about building (on pitch) momentum. And I think that's something that Doncaster have really struggled with. They win a game, then lose two. That's why they are where they are at the minute.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Ruben Amorim urged AC Milan to find consistency across all competitions as they look to turn around their dire Europa League form.

Milan travel to Olympiacos for their fifth league-phase game in Europe, with Amorim's side sitting 28th in the 36-team table, but just one point off the play-offs.

That is in contrast to their returns in Serie A, where Milan are fourth after three straight wins, including a 5-1 victory over Frosinone last time out.

Milan have won just one of their four Europa League games so far, though (L3), losing each of the last two to Bournemouth (3-0) and Ferencvaros (2-0).

They have never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net before, and Amorim says Milan cannot be classed as a good team unless they show it on all fronts.

"To be a good team, you have to do well both in the league and in Europe," insisted Amorim.

According to recent reports, "That's the only way to be a good team. We have to be, especially at Milan. I'm always waiting for things to go badly, because it doesn't take much to change the situation.

Sources indicate that "That's what I'm trying to make my players understand, because it won't always be this way. We're at the beginning of a process, and I think we need everyone.

In a recent development, "We lost [Aleksandar] Pavlovic, [Luka] Modric, [Alexis] Saelemaekers, [Samuel] Chukwueze, and everyone has to be ready, because there are no excuses at big clubs. We have to be ready for this. I can't believe we lost all these games in Europe because we rotated.

"We have to always be ready and approach the games like against Inter, Frosinone, and Genoa. We're building so many things. [It] is another test for us.".

A last tune-up before we head to Greece Brought to you by @play_eFootball https://t.co/ifI9S3vgMG.

— AC Milan (@acmilan) November 25, 2026.

Milan have never won a major European away match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

They have netted four goals in the Europa League this term, but all of those came away to Salzburg in a single match.

"It's a fact that we need to improve in the final third," Amorim added.

In a recent development, "The only thing we can do is improve our principles. We need to improve on these little things, and that's the only way I can help my players.

"Against Olympiacos, it will be a different match than the one against Frosinone, just as it will be different than the one against Cagliari.

Recent findings suggest that "We need to improve, even in our defending. We've almost always conceded a goal, so that's another area we need to improve.".

Mikel Arteta provided a coy upgrade on David Raya’s availability for Arsenal’s showdown with Manchester City this weekend.

Kepa has had limited football since joining the club, so trusted has Raya become for Arsenal, but Arteta insisted he will have full faith in the goalkeeper if he is required to start in goal against City.

  • Braga will look to strengthen their position in the Conference League knockout-stage race when they welcome KuPS Kuopio to the Estadio Municipal de Braga on Thursday evening.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 24 Nov 2026 19:40.

Braga will look to strengthen their position in the Conference League knockout-stage race when they welcome KuPS Kuopio to the Estadio Municipal de Braga on Thursday evening.

Franclim Carvalho's side are 17th in the 36-team standings with four points from three matches, while the Finnish visitors sit 33rd with just one point after failing to win any of their opening three European outings.

Despite going unbeaten in their six matches across three Conference League qualifying rounds (W4, D2) and keeping clean sheets in all of them, Braga have found life in the league phase considerably more challenging.

The Archbishops began their campaign with a disappointing 3-0 defeat away to Copenhagen before responding with a 2-0 home victory over Gent on matchday two, giving Carvalho his first win since replacing the sacked Carlos Vicens in October.

However, Braga were unable to build on that success in their latest continental outing, playing out a goalless draw away to Aarhus, although the upcoming manager can take encouragement from the defensive improvements made in recent times.

The Portuguese outfit are unbeaten in their last four matches across all competitions, keeping clean sheets in each and winning three, with their latest success coming in a 2-0 victory away to Vitoria de Guimaraes in the Taca de Portugal at the weekend.

That result followed a 1-0 league win at Rio Ave, leaving Braga eighth in the Primeira Liga table with 17 points from their opening 11 fixtures and three points adrift of the top five.

The Archbishops are also three points away from fifth place in the Conference League standings, with several teams between 10th and 14th sitting just two points ahead, meaning maximum points on Thursday could strengthen their hopes of securing a top-eight finish.

Braga have plenty of reason to feel confident ahead of the contest, having won 14 of their last 16 home matches in European competition (D1, L1) and kept 12 clean sheets during that run.

KuPS, meanwhile, have struggled to make an impression in their second consecutive Conference League league-phase campaign, losing 4-2 to Trabzonspor in their opening fixture before suffering a 2-0 defeat away to Borac Banja Luka on matchday two.

The Finnish side collected their first point with a goalless draw against Gent on matchday three, but that result did little to disguise their attacking struggles, having scored just twice and conceded six goals across their opening three matches in the competition.

Miika Nuutinen's men have also gone seven matches without a victory, including a 1-1 draw against Swedish side Norrkoping in a friendly on November 19, while their most recent competitive outing was a 2-0 home defeat to Inter Turku in their final match of the 2026 top-flight campaign.

That result left the Yellow-Blacks third in the Veikkausliiga table, meaning they missed out on retaining the domestic title they won last season but secured a place in the first qualifying round of the Conference League.

KuPS have also struggled on their travels, recording just one victory in their last eight competitive away matches and failing to win any of their most recent four, three of which ended in defeat.

Braga will be without Sikou Niakate, who is recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon that has kept him sidelined since April.

Jonas Wind is also doubtful after missing the recent victory over Vitoria because of physical overload, while Gabriel Silva returned as a second-half substitute at the weekend after missing the previous four matches through fitness problems and could feature again as he builds up his match fitness.

Fran Navarro ended a more than three-month wait for a goal by scoring against Vitoria and is expected to retain his place at the head of the attack, with club captain Ricardo Horta and Pau Victor also likely to feature in Carvalho's forward line.

KuPS could be without 22-year-old Ghanaian winger Bob Nii Armah, who picked up an injury during the goalless draw with Gent.

Thirty-three-year-old attacker Piotr Parzyszek has started all three of the Finnish side's league-phase matches and could retain his place despite failing to score in his last 10 competitive appearances for the club.

Morocco FA confirm appeal intends after Senegal awarded AFCON 2025 title

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Moroccan FA say they blueprint to explore all legal avenues to appeal after expressing their “protest” against the CAS ruling to reinstate Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners.
  • Sources indicate that while Senegal won 1-0 against Morocco in the final of AFCON 2025, the match was beset by controversy.
  • But African football governing body CAF retrospectively awarded the title to Morocco two months after the final, stating that Senegal’s conduct during the match had disqualified them as winners.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Moroccan FA say they blueprint to explore all legal avenues to appeal after expressing their “protest” against the CAS ruling to reinstate Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners.

Sources indicate that while Senegal won 1-0 against Morocco in the final of AFCON 2025, the match was beset by controversy. Senegal players and staff left the pitch in the 98th minute in protest against the award of a penalty for the hosts, which left the game paused for 14 minutes. The match eventually resumed, Brahim Diaz missed the spot kick and the game went to extra time, which saw Senegal score and go on to lift the trophy.

But African football governing body CAF retrospectively awarded the title to Morocco two months after the final, stating that Senegal’s conduct during the match had disqualified them as winners. Morocco were named automatic 3-0 winners.

The Senegalese FA took an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) which, after a months-long saga, reinstated Senegal as champions on Tuesday.

But Morocco have not given up, citing reports of an alleged telephone conversation between CAS panelist Ulrich Haas and the president of Senegal’s football federation hours before Tuesday’s ruling as one reason they have grounds for an appeal.

The CAS ruling said: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated.

“Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).

“By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.

“In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

“Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.”.

Senegal awarded Afcon 2025 title by CAS verdict as Morocco stripped.

But Morocco have vowed to appeal CAS’s ruling.

Sources indicate that A statement from the Moroccan FA stated: “We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to recent reports, in the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

Sources indicate that the vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

It has been revealed that on top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding latest levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Industry observers note that needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

Industry observers note that I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Recent findings suggest that then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around rapidly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:47.
  • Seeking to bounce back from a rare Premier League defeat, Brighton & Hove Albion welcome Universitatea Craiova to the Amex Stadium for matchday four in the Conference League on Thursday night.
  • Both teams have identical records in the League Phase, collecting seven points courtesy of two wins and one draw from their first three games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:47.

Seeking to bounce back from a rare Premier League defeat, Brighton & Hove Albion welcome Universitatea Craiova to the Amex Stadium for matchday four in the Conference League on Thursday night.

Both teams have identical records in the League Phase, collecting seven points courtesy of two wins and one draw from their first three games.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw in seven Premier League games, Brighton came away from the MKM Stadium stunned after conceding two stoppage-time goals to lose 2-0 away against Hull City on Sunday.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler rued his side’s “missed opportunity which can't happen again” after seeing leaders Arsenal and Man City also drop points over the weekend. Brighton still sit between both clubs in second place in the table, six points behind the Gunners and level on points with City in third.

Brighton have scored a whopping 40 goals in 18 games across all competitions this term, but the goals have dried up slightly in recent weeks; they have drawn a blank in front of goal in three of their last seven games and have scored at least twice on just two occasions during this run.

While the prospect of qualifying for next season’s Champions League via their domestic performances has become a distinct possibility, Brighton also have aspirations of winning their first-ever major trophy and following in the footsteps of Crystal Palace, West Ham and Chelsea in winning the Conference League this term.

The Seagulls, who secured a narrow 1-0 win over Getafe in Spain three weeks ago, presently sit fifth in the 36-team League Phase standings and could consolidate their place in the top eight with a victory on Thursday.

Should they beat Craiova without reply, they will become just the third English team this century to prevail in five consecutive European home games without conceding a goal.

Universitatea Craiova narrowly missed out on a place in the Conference League knockout rounds last season, finishing outside the top-24 positions on goal difference after accumulating seven points from six matches.

However, the White-Blues have already picked up the same number of points in half as many games so far this season and sit eighth in the table, leaving them well-placed to secure a historic first-ever appearance in the knockout stages of UEFA competition and potentially bypass the playoff round altogether.

After holding Getafe to a 1-1 draw on matchday one, Filipe Coelho’s side have since celebrated back-to-back wins over Andorran outfit Inter Escaldes (3-1) and Albanian team Egnatia (1-0) – they have not won three consecutive European games since a four-match streak in the 1984 UEFA Cup.

Craiova travel to the South Coast of England in superb form, having put together an impressive 15-game unbeaten run in all tournaments (W11 D4), most recently winning 6-2 against UTA Arad last weekend to retain their position at the top of the Romanian Superliga table.

Recent findings suggest that femi Azeez was “available” to face Hull at the weekend but was not selected in the matchday squad. The summer signing from Millwall recently recovered from a thigh injury and could be ready to make his long-awaited debut for the Seagulls on Thursday.

Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood has scored each of his last five goals for Brighton on home soil and could be recalled to the first XI along with the likes of Ferdi Kadioglu, Mats Wieffer, Ibrahim Osman and Charalampos Kostoulas.

As for Universitatea Craiova, Monday Etim (muscle) and Pavlo Isenko (knee) are both ruled out with injuries, while Mihnea Radulescu is ineligible for the Conference League.

Coelho is expected to stick with a 3-4-3 formation, with Oleksandr Romanchuk, Nikola Stevanovic and Vladimir Screciu set to continue in a three-man backline as Nicusor Bancu and Carlos Mora operating as wing-backs.

Stefan Baiaram scored a brace at the weekend and could retain his starting spot on the left side of attack, while Simon Elisor and Assad Al-Hamlawi have both netted 11 goals this season and will battle it out for a start up front.

Universitatea Craiova possible starting lineup:.

Popescu; Romanchuk, Stevanovic, Screciu; Mora, Baluta, Cicaldau, Bancu; Matei, Al Hamlawi, Baiaram.

As the only team yet to concede in this season’s Conference League, and with nine of their last 10 home outings seeing at least one side fail to score, Brighton possess the defensive solidity to frustrate an in-form Craiova attack.

The Romanian leaders are set for by far their sternest examination on the continent, and even if Hurzeler opts to shuffle his pack, the Seagulls should have more than enough quality to claim a routine victory.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jack Hinshelwood says Brighton must fine-tune some of the aspects of their defeat to Hull City in the Premier League when they return to Conference League action.

Brighton welcome Universitatea Craiova to the AMEX Stadium on Thursday fresh from losing 2-0 against Sergej Jakirovic's side late on thanks to Oli McBurnie's double.

The result saw the Seagulls miss the chance to close the gap to Premier League leaders Arsenal, with the gap now six points between the top two teams in England.

However, Brighton are now turning their attention to Europe and securing a spot in the top eight of the Conference League table against their Romanian opponents.

Brighton have won their last four major European games at home without conceding and could become just the third English side this century to win 5+ home European games in a row without conceding after Tottenham (W5 in 2020-2021) and Chelsea (W5 in 2021-2022).

The Seagulls will face a Romanian side for the first time, and Hinshelwood wants to see a response in Brighton's next two games, with Newcastle United up next on Sunday.

According to recent reports, "We are second in the Premier League and undefeated in the Conference League. We are a difficult side to play against, and to beat," Hinshelwood told reporters.

"The Conference League is different from the Premier League; teams tend to sit deep against us, making it harder to break them down, which is why we drew 0-0 with Jablonec and had a tough time securing a win against Getafe.

"The performance [in Sunday's defeat against Hull] wasn't terrible – there are definitely parts we need to fine-tune and hold ourselves accountable for – but it's notable that we show a good reaction this Thursday and Sunday with two massive games at home.".

Back under the lights in Europe… https://t.co/L2D6nfm1aW.

— Brighton & Hove Albion (@BHAFC) November 25, 2026.

Brighton have kept a clean sheet in 73% of their major European games (8/11), including all three matches in the Conference League this season – it is the highest such rate among sides to play 5+ games on the European stage.

However, they come up against a Craiova side that have made a solid start to their campaign, sitting level on points with Brighton but three places below them on goal difference.

Craiova have won their last two games in the Conference League and will be looking to win three in a row in major European competitions for the first time since a four-game streak in the UEFA Cup in 1984.

And Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler warned his players against complacency, saying: "[Universitatea Craiova] are a good side – they have seven points, just like us – and they play good football.

In a recent development, "The way Craiova plays is impressive; we shouldn't underestimate them. They play with a back three and two defensive midfielders.

"Their wingers are very good, and their striker is excellent. They are strong both with and without the ball.".

Thierry Henry believes Arsenal can end Manchester City’s title hopes this weekend.

Mikel Arteta’s table-topping champions take on Enzo Maresca’s struggling contenders on Sunday, November 29, with six points presently separating the two sides.

As such, victory for Arsenal would extend the margin between the Gunners and City to nine points after 12 games.

Henry is predicting his former side to “dominate” City, despite a stuttering return to action, with draws with Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund, since returning from the international break.

Industry observers note that he told CBS Sports: “You have two teams who have to rectify two things at the weekend. Arsenal, like we’ve been saying recently, and Mikel Arteta has been saying, when you’re on top of a team, don’t let them come back to attack like we’ve seen in the last two games.

Sources indicate that "If you go back to City, and I’ve said it since the beginning of the season, the balance of the team isn’t right. Simple as that.

"They have quality, they have goalscorers who will bail them out, Rayan Cherki bailed them out [against Napoli] but the cohesion of the team, the way they don’t stop counters, they don't control the game on and off the ball like they used to.

"That didn't stop them losing games under Pep [Guardiola] but they were more in control of games.

"You have two teams who have been dominating the league in the last two, three years. But I want to see an Arsenal team that's going to dominate City, and they are there to be dominated.

"But on the other side, it might be the day that City wake up. But if they play the same way they’ve been playing recently, being open and all over the place in midfield, it could be a long day.".

Jamie Carragher agreed with his CBS Sports colleague, adding: "I think Arsenal will win. I can’t see City getting anything from that game.

"They’ve been really poor of late, the results have shown that, not strong defensively at all.

"And that's not because Arsenal are amazing. Listen, they are a top team, don’t get me wrong, but in terms of the Champions League, I don’t think the Premier League teams can match… only Arsenal can really match what we’re seeing from the top teams.”.

Carragher went on to argue that Arsenal’s proven strength in the Champions League automatically made the Gunners favourites for a second Premier League crown in two years.

“For the Premier League not to have more than one, considering we’ve got five in the competition and the funds they all have, it’s probably a bit disappointing and demonstrates why Arsenal are favourites for the Premier League.".

Industry News: Aberdeen boss Mario Frick's heavy metal football is music to the ears of their long-suffering supporters

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1245 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 23 November 2026.

As they embarked on the long journey home from Kilmarnock on Saturday night, Aberdeen supporters would surely have felt a little extra spring in their step.

If 2026 felt like it had been shaping up to be something of an annus horribilis, a 4-2 victory at Rugby Park undoubtedly lifted some of the gloom that had been hanging over the club these past few months.

Industry observers note that granted, a sample size of only one match under Mario Frick is very small. Nobody would be of a mind to get carried away with themselves just yet, especially given that Killie are easily the worst team in the league.

But there was enough in the performance, particularly during a first half which saw them score three goals in 30 minutes, to suggest that a brighter future could lie ahead under the new manager.

Recent findings suggest that aberdeen were aggressive, they played on the front foot, and they attacked with pace. Most of all, they were actually exciting and entertaining to watch.

Those were boxes they never ticked at any point during Stephen Robinson's time in charge. Robinson failed at Aberdeen and his team were routinely awful in terms of the quality of football they served up.

Mario Frick celebrates after a 4-2 win over Kilmarnock in his first game as Aberdeen manager.

Ante Palaversa is back in the Aberdeen team after becoming the forgotten man of Pittodrie.

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet rediscovered the feelgood factor by scoring twice at Rugby Park.

In the space of only 90 minutes, Frick did more to send a wave of positivity through supporters than Robinson ever managed to do in his eight months at the helm.

The shift in mood has been as profound as it has been instantaneous, with Frick's so-called heavy metal football music to the fans' ears.

Headlines of Super Mario were always likely to follow, but Frick and his players will face an altogether tougher examination when they take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow.

It is an intriguing contest on various levels, with Rangers unbeaten in 13 matches as Derek McInnes goes up against his former club once again.

Given that these teams met in the Premier Sports Cup only a few weeks ago, perhaps the greatest barometer of Frick's impact will be whether Aberdeen can pose more of a threat than they did at Hampden.

But what has changed? After such a turgid run of form that left players looking completely bereft of any confidence and cohesion, how was Frick able to generate an immediate improvement?

Speaking after the win at Killie, Frick was asked what sort of message he had given to the players given that time together on the training pitch had been fairly limited.

In a recent development, 'I told them they should play like they did when they were young. In those days they didn't think about mistakes.

'They didn't think about anything negative. They played only to win, for fun.'.

It was simple but refreshing. In an age of increasingly complex coaching jargon, Frick's message was intended to liberate his players – and it worked a treat.

Recent findings suggest that aberdeen went 2-0 up inside 12 minutes, with Kevin Nisbet scoring twice. The team looked free from the trauma of the Robinson era.

Even when Kilmarnock fought back and the game became more chaotic, Aberdeen retained enough attacking threat and collective belief to close it out.

It was a huge result. A defeat would have dropped Aberdeen to the foot of the table. Instead, they climbed five places and, more importantly, rediscovered a feelgood factor.

In his previous utterances, Frick was clear that goalscoring has been the central problem.

His previous teams at Vaduz and Luzern were known for their attacking output. At Luzern last season they scored 76 goals.

Sources indicate that aberdeen had managed only 12 in 12 league matches before his arrival. The early evidence suggests the players have absorbed the message quickly.

Frick's insistence on the basics – aggression, willingness to work, positive body language – appears to have cut through more effectively than more elaborate instructions might have done.

Recent findings suggest that this is consistent with the picture painted by those who worked with him in Switzerland. Frick is not a rigid systems coach wedded to a single formation.

In a recent development, he has most often used a 4-4-2 diamond, but the shape is secondary to the mentality. High pressing to force turnovers, rapid counter-attacks, and a sense of freedom imbued to his players.

All of which makes tomorrow's clash at Ibrox all the more compelling. Aberdeen have lost their last eight meetings with Rangers in all competitions.

The previous two encounters this season, one in the Premiership and one in the Premier Sports Cup, were both settled by late Rangers goals.

Industry observers note that the contrast in styles will be stark. Rangers are likely to control territory and force Aberdeen to defend for longer periods than they did at Rugby Park.

Frick's side will need to show that the freedom he has granted them does not dissolve into naivety when the opponent is stronger and more experienced.

The high press that worked so effectively against a struggling Killie side will have to be timed with greater precision.

The attacking play will require clinical decision-making in the final third. And the defensive structure, which Frick identified as the main area for improvement after Saturday, will be examined under more sustained pressure.

Frick has already spoken of aiming higher than mere survival. In a league which is always extremely tight in the mid-table, top six should be the minimum target.

Sources indicate that that may have sounded optimistic a fortnight ago. But the win at Kilmarnock suggested Aberdeen have enough about themselves to be looking up rather than over their shoulders.

The squad still needs greater consistency and, in certain areas, greater quality.

But there is already evidence to suggest he can get a tune out of some players who either under-performed under Robinson or, in some cases, those who had been totally discarded.

Ante Palaversa would surely be chief among them. The Croatian midfielder hardly kicked a ball under Robinson and had become the forgotten man at Pittodrie.

Brought in to make his first league start of the season, his performance at Killie and the way he controlled things in midfield made his exclusion under Robinson look all the more bizarre.

According to recent reports, none of this is to say that Aberdeen are suddenly a top-class football team. At best, they remain very much a work in progress.

Yet, crucially, Frick immediately has the supporters onboard in a way that Robinson never managed to do.

Frick and his players could yet be given a major reality check if they were to suffer a hefty defeat to a Rangers side unbeaten in 13 matches.

But there is belief and positivity in the camp at Pittodrie. Feelgood factors in football can often be fragile and often short-lived, but they are also real.

When players begin to play with freedom and confidence, results usually tend to take care of themselves.

Frick has not yet transformed Aberdeen. He has, however, given the players and the fans a reason to believe that a brighter future could lie ahead.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rasmus Hojlund made clear that his allegiances remain tied to Manchester United after scoring for Napoli against Manchester City on Tuesday night.

The Denmark international helped his side record a 2-2 draw at the Etihad in the Champions League, opening the scoring in the 55th minute.

In his celebration he gestured with one finger up and before shouted out: “There’s only one club in Manchester”.

Asked after the game about the celebration, Hojlund confirmed: “Yeah I did. Some good banter, you know.

“There’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and obviously I have a past in Manchester United. That’s my club. Nothing against City but United is my home.

“It was good to score here, a good point - happy for that.”.

Hojlund joined Manchester United in the summer of 2023 from Atalanta in a deal worth up to £72million.

Arsenal are still sweating on the fitness of David Raya as they prepare for a crunch run of fixtures that begins with Sunday’s visit of Manchester City in the Premier League.

The Gunners were rocked by an injury to their influential first-choice goalkeeper during the latter stages of last weekend’s eventful 2-2 draw with Newcastle after he hurt his shoulder during an initially innocuous-looking collision with William Osula.

Raya sat out Tuesday’s lively home draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, with unconvincing deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga stepping in from the start ahead of No3 Illan Meslier.

Mikel Arteta will be desperate to have the reigning Golden Glove winner back for a crucial stretch of games that sees Arsenal also take on the likes of Tottenham, Real Madrid and Manchester United before Christmas.

With that massive showdown against title rivals City coming up at the Emirates Stadium, here is all the latest Arsenal injury news and return dates, with William Saliba now back and Max Dowman having served his suspension.

Raya was in considerable pain after colliding with Osula at St James’ Park and had to go off after receiving treatment, with his left arm placed in a protective sling before he was promptly sent for scans.

He was seen still wearing that sling while out in London the next day and was then absent from Arsenal’s open training session at London Colney on Monday morning.

Arteta said that he would definitely miss the Dortmund game, but soothed fan fears by stating that the injury was “not too serious” following “encouraging” test results and did not require surgery, raising hopes that he would be in a position to make a quick return against City.

A new patch was expected following the draw with Dortmund, when Arteta was coy on if Raya would be involved at the weekend.

It has been revealed that “No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately,” Arteta said. “We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].”.

Saka has yet to resume training and when asked about his recovery before the Newcastle game, Arteta suggested that he was likely to miss another month.

Quizzed on if Saka would be available for Manchester United’s visit to north London just before Christmas, the manager said: “I cannot be that specific. In four weeks’ time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five.

"He's out," Arteta said of Zubimendi last week. “Unfortunately he has a slight problem in his hamstring.

After Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing at the hands of Liverpool, the Red Devils now possess the most porous rearguard in any of Europe’s top five leagues.

Michael Carrick’s successor was given an instant reality check at Anfield and is now fully aware of the size of the task he faces with United entrenched in the relegation zone after 11 matches.

Pochettino attempted to shake things up defensively yesterday with Matthijs de Ligt handed a surprise start, but the Netherlands international, still feeling his way back from a long-term injury, was given the run around by Liverpool’s spritely attack.

Leny Yoro, meanwhile, was sent-off after just eight minutes and the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot also hardly covered themselves in glory in the face of relentless pressure from Andoni Iraola’s side.

Despite the obvious defensive concerns, the other end of the pitch represents equal concern for Pochettino.

United opted against signing a newly introduced forward in the summer window, a decision that has spectacularly backfired given the setbacks encountered by Benjamin Sesko.

The Slovenia international displayed signs of promise after a difficult start to his United career last season following his £74million move from RB Leipzig.

A nagging shin injury has restricted the 23-year-old to just six appearances so far this term and he is unlikely to return until the New Year at the earliest.

United’s brains trust has just over a month to consider their options when it comes to recruiting a latest forward.

Folarin Balogun, the Monaco striker, wants to be reunited with Pochettino, who coached the former Arsenal player during his tenure as USA head coach.

‘I think my point of view was very clear.’.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has said that his future is currently "not vital".

Fernandes, 32, only has a contract with the Red Devils until the end of the campaign, but the club do have the option to extend it for a further 12 months.

The Portugal international has reportedly rejected Man United's latest offer, allegedly wanting a longer deal with higher wages given his contribution during a tough period.

There is currently speculation surrounding his future at Old Trafford, but Fernandes has insisted that his main focus for the moment is on helping Man United to turn their campaign around.

Fernandes also refused to "close the door" on returning to Sporting before the end of his career.

"I will never close the door to [returning to] Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart," the Man United captain added.

The Portuguese represented Sporting between 2017 and 2020 ahead of a move to Man United, scoring 63 goals and registering 50 assists in 137 appearances for the club.

Since arriving at Man United, Fernandes has a record of 113 goals and 111 assists in 342 appearances for the English team in all competitions.

Fernandes is again expected to be in the starting side when the Red Devils tackle Sporting in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

  • Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:30 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 17:03 EST, 23 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to buy Manchester United out of trouble in the January transfer window.

Pochettino admitted that United are in a relegation battle after a painful 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge left the club second from bottom of the Premier League.

It’s understood the Argentine will have a limited budget well under £50million with United’s hands tied by the league’s latest financial rules. Pochettino is only expected to make two new signings in January, even if one of them is a loan deal.

Sources have not ruled out the possibility of United gambling if there is a genuine threat of the club being relegated for the first time in 53 years, but they would still have to spend responsibly.

The defeat to Liverpool underlined the need for Pochettino to strengthen in central defence, with Brentford’s Nathan Collins emerging as a strong candidate ahead of Calvin Bassey, who is expected to sign a new contract with Fulham, and Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite who is valued at over £70million.

In a recent development, united also want a left-back after failing to sign cover for Luke Shaw in the summer when they were linked with Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Rayan Ait-Nouri of Manchester City. Both those players could be potential targets again.

Mauricio Pochettino will have less than £50million to try and fix Manchester United in January.

Pochettino is only expected to make two latest signings in January - pictured: Chief executive Omar Berrada (left) and director of football Jason Wilcox (centre).

Pochettino would also like a new striker after Benjamin Sesko’s shin injury left him short of firepower until the New Year.

Monaco’s Folarin Balogun, who played under Pochettino for the US national team, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ivan Toney, the former Brentford centre-forward now playing for Al-Ahli, have all been linked with a move to Old Trafford.

However, Toney’s £500,000-a-week wages put him out of United’s reach, and Leeds are keen to extend Calvert-Lewin’s contract which is worth £180,000-a-week.

Meanwhile, United are appealing to the FA over Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool.

Industry observers note that yoro was sent off in the eighth minute at Anfield for a challenge on Alexander Isak on the edge of the penalty box. The Frenchman was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott, and Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s first goal from the free-kick.

However, United insist that Yoro did not deny Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity because goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the ball first.

The club have notified the FA of their intention to appeal in the hope of having Yoro’s one-match ban overturned so he can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Steven Gerrard admits he is struggling to understand Xabi Alonso’s refusal to utilise one of Chelsea’s key summer signings.

After some encouraging early signs, the Blues have fallen off the title pace being set by Arsenal and have suffered several damaging defeats in recent weeks.

A rare home loss against Tottenham was compounded by Saturday’s drubbing at the hands of Leeds United at Stamford Bridge when defensive shortcomings were to the fore once again.

Alonso has refused to use injuries as an excuse for an alarming dip in form but the absences of Reece James and Joao Pedro are being keenly felt.

The Brazil international striker is particularly key component of Chelsea’s system, but cover was sourced during the summer window in the shape of the experienced Danny Welbeck.

Alonso, however, has appeared strangely reluctant to start the 35-year-old in Pedro’s absence, with Pedro Neto preferred on occasion while against Leeds he chose to hand a starting opportunity to the largely untried Emmanuel Emegha.

‘Especially with Joao Pedro out, you’re thinking it’s perfect for Danny Welbeck, and he’s an experienced player out there,’ Gerrard told The Overlap with Sky Bet when asked about his former England teammate.

‘He’s someone who can help a lot of youngsters that are playing, a lot of inexperienced players at Chelsea.

‘Same reason why they brought in Jordan Henderson, and you would say that Jordan’s done a really good job, what Xabi Alonso’s wanted him to do, but with no Joao Pedro, to not see hardly anything of Welbeck is a major surprise.

‘But from the Welbeck we watched at Brighton & Hove Albion, what was it, three, four months ago, the back end of last season, you would think he would be the perfect replacement for Joao Pedro being missing for such a period of time.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

In a recent development, I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Another chastening week in the unhinged world of Chelsea has shown Xabi Alonso that the thing he most craves is what his team lack more than anything.

Managers are neurotic creatures and Alonso’s great obsession is “control”, which you’d have to say is rather concerning from what we have seen of his tenure so far.

Ask the Spaniard to name his favourite performance from Chelsea’s opening 11 games of the Premier League season and he will cite last month’s 2-0 away win over Everton. A rare victory up north delivered a first top-flight clean sheet since January and, more importantly, was professional and diligent.

There is a time and a place for football as entertainment, but Alonso is in a results-based business and knows, from his unbeaten campaign leading Bayer Leverkusen to Bundesliga glory, that the less memorable wins are key to building a team in control of its destiny, delivering consistent results.

Chelsea are many things; they are not that.

The club were understandably excited in the summer when they secured their first-choice candidate, and appointing Alonso as manager, not head coach, has given the impression that he has more control in the overall running of first-team operations than his recent predecessors.

Sources indicate that that is not translating to the pitch, though. Far from it. In every area of the field, control is absent without leave.

Four months in, Xabi Alonso is yet to imprint his identity on Chelsea.

According to recent reports, joao Pedro’s thigh injury has left Chelsea hamstrung in attack. Cole Palmer looks lost and ineffectual; Morgan Rogers is left carrying an excessive burden.

According to recent reports, the performances with and without another player, Moises Caicedo, are just as strikingly worlds apart from each other. An overreliance on the Ecuadorian has set alarm bells ringing for months.

The constant need for one midfielder to fill in alongside the centre-backs leaves Chelsea brutally outnumbered in the middle of the park, just as in the defeats by Brentford and Tottenham.

Both before and since Maxence Lacroix’s untimely injury, Alonso has been so unable to trust Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana that 20-year-old Josh Acheampong has proven the only broadly solid defender.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal learn £100m twist; new Man Utd target.

Fofana risks Chelsea fan fury as he laughs off criticism: ‘Couldn’t care less’.

Chelsea handed Joao Pedro warning ahead of £100m transfer decision.

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style.

Chopping and changing between a back three and back four is merely a product of Alonso’s desperation to find a defensive unit that works, yet it has been an enemy to that search for control.

Chelsea have seen little of the ball in some games, but the early wins over Fulham and Brighton came through slick play in transition, and Alonso believes control is not just about slow and steady possession.

“We have spells where I would like us to have better control, and I’m not meaning just control with the ball,” he explained.

Recent findings suggest that “You can have control without the ball when you feel comfortable [because] you know the opponent has the ball where you want them to have it. Then you feel in control. That is the way I like to play.”.

Yet there remains a huge disparity between Alonso’s vision of control without the ball and Chelsea’s actual reality.

Industry observers note that teams are consistently occupying the ball in very dangerous areas and creating the better chances. Leeds, for example, could have scored far more than four on Saturday.

Scoring 20 goals and conceding the same number doesn’t spell control, and it is the first time in a decade that Chelsea have lost as many as five of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Friday night against Nottingham Forest must be more like that mature win at Everton with less of the chaos seen from Chelsea since.

According to recent reports, alonso was considered the brightest newly introduced tactical mind in management less than two years ago, but is yet to imprint his identity on Chelsea four months in. He is not under immediate pressure of the sack, but grace periods don’t last forever.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans should not expect much transfer business to be done this winter, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to be given a meagre budget to work with in January.

The Argentine has arrived as the new Red Devils boss and took charge of his first game on Sunday, which did not go well at all as Liverpool romped to a 4-0 win over their old rivals at Anfield.

Leny Yoro was shown an early red card, leaving Pochettino’s plans in tatters as defeat left Manchester United 19th in the Premier League table.

With just one win and 23 goals conceded in 11 league outings, there have been calls for signings to be made, especially in defence.

Before Pochettino was appointed, club legend Gary Neville even urged him to turn down the job unless the hierarchy promised to sign two defenders over the winter transfer window.

That may still happen, but it will have to be some canny business as the Daily Mail reports that Manchester United will have ‘well under £50 million’ to spend in the next transfer window.

Having focused on midfield signings over the summer, United want a centre-back, left-back and striker, but obviously that cannot be done to any level of quality on such a meagre budget.

Brentford centre-back Nathan Collins has been touted as a target, but the 25-year-old would not be a cheap option.

The Bees paid £23m for him when they signed him from Wolves three years ago and he remains under contract until 2029.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The Republic of Ireland international has been a mainstay in the team since moving to Brentford, although is currently out with injury.

Summer targets at left-back included Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri and Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, both of whom could be options again.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been linked with a move to Old Trafford, having worked with Pochettino in his stint as USA manager.

The former Arsenal man came close to joining Everton in a £40m deal over the summer before the deal collapsing at the last minute.

Manchester United may look to make a loan signing to keep costs down, although could stretch the budget if they feel that relegation is a genuine threat.

Neville does not think it will come to a relegation scrap, despite United’s woeful form, saying after the defeat to Liverpool: ‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight. They’re second-bottom in the league, it’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years. I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.

Recent findings suggest that however, he added: ‘You could arrogantly look at Coventry at home, or Sunderland at home, and think United will be alright. But the performance levels we’re seeing at the moment don’t give you much confidence.’.
