📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adrien Rabiot has had an outstanding start to the 2026-27 season, and he is showing absolutely no signs of slowing down.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by pointing out what Rabiot remarked after Milan’s 5-1 demolition of Frosinone on Sunday: “An assist is better than a goal.” He was the man of the match against Frosinone: five goals were scored, yet none bore his name.

Still, the Frenchman made himself the stand-out performer, thanks to his tireless running, leadership, and a series of decisive passes, not to mention his role in the opening goal, which came via an own-goal.

It was a summer of doubts for Rabiot, given that his extended vacation was interpreted by some as a sign of discontent and a longing to reunite with his former mentor – Massimiliano Allegri – at Napoli. Yet, he has transformed into a cornerstone of this newly introduced era.

It has been revealed that the former PSG man is now a decisive force on the pitch, integral to Ruben Amorim’s tactical framework, and a true leader. The numbers demonstrate this perfectly: Rabiot is the first midfielder to contribute to at least one goal (scoring or assisting) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004.

With five goals and six assists, he recently became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A to record more than 10 goal contributions within the first 10 matches of a single season. In total, Rabiot has surpassed the milestone of 50 direct goal involvements in Serie A (29 goals and 22 assists).

Milan trust him, and the feeling is mutual. As previously mentioned, the very fact that he remained with the Rossoneri over the summer – publicly reaffirming his commitment to the club – is reflected in his attitude, both on and off the field.

Adrien Rabiot – Goal Contributions so far.

12 G/A in 14 Games https://t.co/s8oTle9GBn.

— c0mp (@c0mpmilano) November 23, 2026.

He is always smiling and highly active on social media; his numbers on Instagram are as impressive as his stats on the field. He posts photos of his goals, his celebrations and embraces with Diego Moreira, with whom he is clearly building a close bond.

Recent findings suggest that amorim said after the game: “Adrien can play as a ’10,’ an attacking midfielder, an ‘8,’ or even as a playmaker – though he doesn’t particularly like that role. He is certainly one of the best players I have ever coached, and one of the best midfielders in Europe.”.

Speaking to Telefoot, Rabiot addressed the topic of his excellent start statistically: “It’s a positive thing to have players capable of being decisive, even if they aren’t forwards. It also serves as an encouragement to those around us.

“At Milan, we have quite a few young players, and it’s important for them to have role models in their day-to-day lives. I had only been back from vacation for a week when he was already talking to me about a contract renewal.

Industry observers note that “I told him, ‘Coach, take it easy!’ (laughs). But, naturally, it’s significant for a player to feel that kind of trust—the coach relies on us, holds us in high regard, and makes us feel important.”.

Further significant remarks regarding Rabiot were made by Gerry Cardinale on the eve of the most recent league match, specifically concerning his imminent contract renewal.

“I love Adrien, he’s one of my favourite players. He’s fantastic. I have enormous respect for him and his family. We are in talks, and I hope we reach a happy conclusion soon. I believe he should be a signature player for Milan. Could it be a Christmas gift for the fans? Absolutely, and for me, too.”.

Sources indicate that the renewal will happen, and it will happen soon. Any delay until the new year should not be interpreted as a negative sign. Rather, it reflects the fact that everything is already settled, and there is no rush to finalise the signature.

Industry observers note that adrien’s current deal – which runs until 2028 – will be extended to 2030, with an additional one-year option. From his current age of 31, he will remain a fixture in the Rossoneri midfield until he is 33 or 34, the prime of his footballing maturity.

Now into his thirties, he will also earn a more lucrative contract than his current one, which pays him €3.5m net per season. It is worth noting that in the summer of 2025, Adrien was acquired from Marseille for €7m after a training-ground altercation with Jonathan Rowe.

It was, by any definition, a fantastic deal. As for the future, Rabiot has a role model he can observe from very close quarters: “Modrić trains as if he were 21, he’s an example to follow. The closer you get to the end of your career, the more you start to savor every moment. I try to do the same.”.

With the imminent contract extension, Adrien Rabiot is also set to conclude his career in the red and black colours, and that would make everyone happy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:31.

Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

Mauricio Pochettino will now take charge of his first European match for Man United, and there is pressure on the Argentine following the four-goal mauling at Anfield.

When asked whether the Sporting match provided Man United with the perfect chance to bounce back from the defeat to Liverpool, Strachan insisted that the players need to show character and heart in a bid to turn the club's campaign around.

According to recent reports, "Well, to be fair, Liverpool should never really be a significant ask for Man United as such, because the record there is terrific over the years. I mean, it's always been decent. That fixture is one of the ones that Liverpool really want to win because they know how dangerous Man United are," stated Strachan.

According to recent reports, "But it wasn't a real game after the first two goals, there was the sending-off, you know. And even the free kick, you think, right, if you see the free kick off, we can reorganise and organise with 10 players. We never even had time to do that. So, as a manager, you can't count that, you've just got to count that as a no-game.

It has been revealed that "But what you can do in that situation is ask, who kept pressing? Who do I want in my team? Because in adversity, you see the real character coming out, and in adversity in major games, you see the real character. And it's not on your social media, it's not saying to the fans, we love you and we're sorry and all the rest of it. Don't apologise to me, just do something about it.

Industry observers note that "Don't come in and hold your hand up and say, I'm sorry, gaffer. Don't apologise to me because I'm not interested in you telling me you're sorry for making a mistake. Just don't make a mistake. And if you do make a mistake, rectify it as quickly as possible.

According to recent reports, "What I'm talking about is managers will try and sort it out. Invariably, unless you can do something about it, physically or mentally, then it will appear again. They will appear, and they'll appear in crisis moments.

According to recent reports, "As I remarked, your character is shown up in crisis times and the same mistakes will be made by the same people whoever they play. And some people are just not good enough to play at this level.

It has been revealed that "You know, we all talk about shapes and systems and this and that. The funny thing is, I don't think there's too many people talking about systems now. I think most people are now talking about, even if you talk with a bright manager, they talk about putting people under pressure, winning knockdowns, getting to the ball first, getting the ball to your front men.

In a recent development, "So, the system thing has kind of changed now. The only one that kind of really changes, it's gone from a back four to a back three, but the rest, like Brighton, Liverpool, Bournemouth, they're all playing the same sort of way.

"It's a kind of 4-2-3-1, where the four players up front are attacking players, whatever way you want to use it, two wide men, just off the front. Wales were the same with Craig Bellamy.

According to recent reports, "So, I think that people are moving to that in general now, but there's not too much talking about systems now. It's more about closing down, getting to knockdowns, winning headers and free kicks and corner kicks.".

Man United have six points to show from their two matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

It has been revealed that asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

According to recent reports, ‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole said of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve mentioned it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’.

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

Rasmus Hojlund has revealed that Bruno Fernandes was among the Manchester United players to be left “devastated” by the recent sacking of Michael Carrick.

Carrick was relieved of his duties as Man Utd boss earlier in November after weeks of intense speculation and less than six months in permanent charge on a two-year contract, with just one win from their opening 10 games having seen his side languish in the Premier League relegation zone.

It is United’s worst start to a top-flight season since 1972, with former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino leaving his role as head coach of the United States national team to rapidly succeed Carrick, only to suffer a chastening 4-0 defeat by arch-rivals Liverpool with 10 men in his first match in charge.

Carrick’s final weeks at United saw senior players air their grievances in public interviews following listless defeats, with Lisandro Martinez taking aim at the club’s recruitment after the loss to Atletico Madrid and Fernandes then questioning Carrick’s tactics in the 4-1 thrashing away at Como.

However, captain and coach were mentioned to have held “clear-the-air talks” and been on good terms before the latter’s dismissal, with Hojlund revealing that Fernandes - along with United and Portugal team-mate Diogo Dalot - had been “devastated” by Carrick’s departure but hopeful of bouncing back promptly under his replacement.

The Danish striker was back in Manchester on Tuesday night in the Champions League, scoring for Napoli against City and making headlines with his pro-United celebration in a lively 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium.

Hojlund previously spent three years at Old Trafford between 2023-26 following a high-profile £72million transfer from Atalanta aged 20, netting 26 times in 95 total appearances across all competitions before returning to Serie A for £38m in the summer as Napoli exercised their option for a permanent deal following a successful season-long loan spell last term.

“In the international break when I spoke with Bruno and Diogo, they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,” stated Hojlund, who recently scored twice for Denmark in their 4-1 thrashing of a Cristiano Ronaldo-less Portugal in the Nations League.

“I am still speaking with [Denmark team-mate and United player] Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best and I am sure they will turn it around this season.”.

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are mentioned to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

It has been revealed that ‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

On his brilliant flicked effort to complete his double, Varela added: ‘It was pure instinct, it’s not something I practice.

‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

‘Sometimes they speak well of me and sometimes they speak badly, but this is the world of football and I only think about what I have to do on the field.’.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

Borussia Dortmund boss Niko Kovac has hailed his side’s fight against “strong” Arsenal, but was frustrated by the decision to deny them a penalty.

BVB drew 1-1 with the Gunners at the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday night after Maximilian Beier’s second-half strike cancelled out an early opening effort by Viktor Gyokeres.

Dortmund repelled waves of dominant but ultimately profligate Arsenal pressure throughout an entertaining league phase encounter but also saw a second goal through Jobe Bellingham ruled out for offside.

A draw despite giving up 30 shots and seeing their woodwork hit three times continued a strong run of form for Dortmund, who presently sit inside the Champions League top eight and above Bayern Munich at the summit of the Bundesliga, having now gone nine games unbeaten across all competitions - winning six.

After the game, Kovac said: “It’s a huge point for us, a huge moment for all of us - for the team and for the fans, who turned out in such major numbers today.

“In the end, of course, we’re happy with the point. The game was here in London, so obviously you have to weather a few dangerous situations.

“I think the team put up a really good fight today. No one would say they were being timid or didn't give it their all. We fought as a team, kept coming back, and highlighted that we can hold our own against a strong opponent.”.

However, Kovac believes that Arsenal were fortunate to avoid giving away a penalty when the ball clearly struck the arm of Gyokeres from a Dortmund corner delivery during the second half.

It has been revealed that “I thought VAR should have looked at the handball. It would have been worth a check,” he noted.

“They are trying to intervene less with the on-field decisions, but it doesn't mean you should not intervene when you should do.

According to recent reports, “I am not crying about it. It is what it is. We got a point. It is a substantial point away to Arsenal, a big one for all of us - our fans, our team and the club.”.

Manchester United have added another experienced Premier League centre-half to their list of targets ahead of the transfer window opening.

After leaking four goals in another humbling defeat at Anfield on Sunday, Mauricio Pochettino has inherited the worst defence in any of Europe’s top five leagues.

Michael Carrick’s successor is mentioned to be keen on adding a striker to his ranks to cover for the injured Benjamin Sesko, but tightening up his backline will also represent a priority.

Fulham’s Calvin Bassey emerged as a potential target last week, but the versatile defender is reported to be close to signing a contract extension with the London club.

According to talkSPORT, United have also identified Brentford’s Nathan Collins as a possible solution to a problem that has plagued successive managers.

The Red Devils also have maintained an interest in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite but he is likely to prove too expensive, given they are reported to have a budget of just £50million to work with.

Collins, 25, is under contract with Brentford until the summer of 2029 and would also command a significant fee.

While reinforcements would certainly aid United’s cause, former club captains Roy Keane and Gary Neville fear it is not just defenders their old side are in need of.

‘My worry for United’s defenders [is] they’re not getting great help,” stated Keane after the Anfield drubbing.

By Freddie Cotton | 24 Nov 2026 20:48, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:58.

Marseille welcome Levski Sofia to the Stade Velodrome on Thursday evening on matchday five of the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Les Olympiens claimed a crucial 1-0 win away to Bayer Leverkusen, while the Blues beat Polish side Jagiellonia by the same scoreline at the National Stadium Vasil Levski.

After narrowly missing out on booking their place in the UEFA Champions League for the second consecutive year last season, finishing fifth in Ligue 1 and just one point below Lyon in fourth, Marseille will be extremely disappointed with how they have performed on the continent so far this campaign.

Although they edged out Leverkusen in their latest Europa League fixture, losses to Sturm Graz, Olympiacos and Besiktas in each of their opening three matches mean Bruno Genesio’s men have earned just three points so far in Europe, leaving them 31st in the league phase table and outside of the knockout stage places.

Despite conceding two late goals to lose against Le Mans on Sunday evening, Les Olympiens have seen a huge improvement in their league endeavours, having won each of their prior five matches to presently sit fifth in the Ligue 1 table and just three points outside the automatic Champions League qualification places.

Marseille are yet to claim victory over Levski, though they do boast a mainly positive record against Bulgarian opposition, having beaten CSKA Sofia in each of their other two meetings with efbet League sides.

Having won their first efbet League title since 2009 last season and finished 10 points ahead of runners-up Ludogorets, who had triumphed in each of the previous 14 consecutive campaigns, Levski competed in the qualifying stages of the Champions League for the first time in 17 years during the summer.

The Blues impressed in their efforts for tournament qualification, beating Borac Banja Luka, Univ Craiova and Kairat Almaty to progress to the decisive playoff tie, but having endured a 4-0 aggregate defeat against Greek giants AEK Athens, the Bulgarian side are instead competing in the Europa League this season.

However, Julio Velazquez’s men have given a good account of themselves so far on the continent as after taking just one point from their first two matches, Levski have won back-to-back matches in the Europa League to sit 10th in the standings with seven points and only outside the round-of-16 positions on goal difference.

While the Blues do not have the best recent record against French opposition, having won just one of their previous four meetings with Ligue 1 sides, that triumph did come over Marseille, with Levski securing a 1-0 win over Les Olympiens in the group stages of this competition in December 2005, when it was branded as the UEFA Cup.

Marseille continue to be without Canadian defender Derek Cornelius, who has been sidelined since the end of September with a hip problem, while former Chelsea full-back Emerson Palmieri is also unavailable due to a knee problem.

On a more positive note, after missing the match against Leverkusen as a precaution, Moroccan forward Amine Harit has started Les Olympiens’ previous two league fixtures and looks set to return to feature from the off in the week too.

Netting eight Ligue 1 goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous four outings, Algerian forward Amine Gouiri is undoubtedly the hosts’ biggest threat going forward and will be hoping to add to his winner against Leverkusen last time out in the competition.

Having been left out of Levski’s Europa League squad list, Oliver Kamdem, Mustapha Sangare and Petko Hristov are all unavailable for Thursday’s fixture, while 34-year-old striker Radoslav Kirilov remains out with a knee issue.

However, the Blues will be delighted to have welcomed midfielder Asen Mitkov back from injury against Lok. Sofia on Sunday afternoon and the 21-year-old will be hopeful for more minutes in the week too.

Contributing to six goals in 12 league appearances, Portuguese midfielder Serginho has been the visitors’ dangerman so far this season and will be hoping to replicate his efbet League form on the continent this week.

While Levski have made a promising start to their campaign, we think Les Olympiens will bag all three points at the Stade Velodrome this week and are backing them to mount a late charge for a top-eight finish in the league phase.

Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

In a recent development, this has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

Sources indicate that this was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage as Newcastle United welcome Aston Villa to St James’ Park in the Premier League.

Newcastle endured a hellish Monday night as they were condemned to an embarrassing 4-1 defeat by Coventry City in their previous top-flight outing. Matthias Jaissle’s rebranded Newcastle outfit have notably lacked consistency in the early weeks of the season, with the loss to Coventry another abrupt reminder of how this is expected to be a challenging campaign for his freshly assembled squad. The upcoming arrivals are yet to fully settle and Newcastle are undoubtedly still adapting following a turbulent summer transfer window where they lost several key players.

Meanwhile, Villa arrive up north in tremendously high spirits following their 6-0 thumping of Fenerbahce in midweek Champions League action, thereby recording their biggest European win in the club’s history. However, in a similar vein to Newcastle, Villa have struggled to impose themselves in the Premier League, triumphing just once in their opening six matches of the season. Unai Emery’s men conceded a 79th-minute equaliser to Brentford’s Kristoffer Ajer last time out in the Premier League to draw 2-2 and deepen their domestic frustration.

Despite how this week’s results have shaped contrasting moods in the two camps, Newcastle are currently three points ahead of Villa in the Premier League, with today’s visitors aiming to make it back-to-back top-flight away wins after beating Tottenham 3-2 in the capital last month.

Industry observers note that jaissle is still trying to find his feet in English football, and hosting Villa is yet another tough test of his credentials. A leaky defence has led to calls from ex-players such as Gary Neville for significant investment, but it appears Man Utd will try to do their business on a tight budget in January.

The second window of the season often leads to inflated prices, with clubs capitalising upon other teams’ struggles and desperate need for newly introduced players.

But there are bargains to be had.

The defence is the priority, with Man Utd reportedly keen on finding a new left-back and centre-back, while Pochettino also wants a new striker.

Fikayo Tomori’s spell at AC Milan looks to be coming to a close at the six-year mark, with the England international caught in the transfer merry-go-round back in the summer.

Massimo Allegri froze the centre-back out of the AC Milan squad, only for the Italian giants to fail in recruiting a replacement. Even when drafted back into the first team, Tomori has found gametime hard to come by - waiting six Serie A games for his first appearance of the league season.

At the moment sidelined with a hamstring issue, GOAL report that Tomori will not be offered a new contract when his current deal expires next summer. Despite being keen on a return to England, the 28-year-old rejected transfers to Fulham and Coventry City.

To save even more money, Man Utd could make a pre-contract agreement with Tomori in January, paving the way for a free transfer next summer.

In a recent development, they cannot do that with Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell, despite the left-back also being out of contract at the end of the season. That is because English clubs cannot agree pre-contracts with players at other teams in England.

As such, Man Utd would have to open up their wallet and spend some cash on the 27-year-old, who has over 200 Premier League games under his belt making his debut during the 2019/20 season.

Such an arrangement would allow Man Utd to spend their money elsewhere, before making a decision on investing further cash into Toney after a loan period.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has refused to confirm whether Luke Shaw will be involved in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon.

Shaw has made the trip to Portugal alongside his teammates, having recovered from the muscular problem that has sidelined him since the early stages of October.

The 31-year-old has been a huge miss at the back for Man United, and Pochettino has welcomed the Englishman's return to fitness.

However, it remains to be seen whether he is involved against Sporting.

“All the players need to feel they can have an impact for the team and they can perform," Pochettino told reporters during his pre-game press conference.

“It’s up to us to give the opportunities to every single player in the moment that we believe that they deserve to be involved in the game.

Industry observers note that “Of course, I know Luke from the past, in our time in Southampton, but all [of us who are] involved, we are not the same people now. It’s more than 10 years ago.

“Obviously, it’s good to see him and he came from a small issue but now he needs to recover his best form.

“It’s good to have him, because he’s experienced everything with the squad, but we’ll see if he can be involved tomorrow or not, from the beginning or during the game.”.

Matheus Cunha is suspended for the match following his red card against Roma in the team's last European fixture, while Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are all injured for the 20-time English champions.

Pochettino also insisted during his press conference that Man United are 'not a fragile team' despite their huge difficulties this season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Maresca signed a contract until June 2029, but he confirmed in a press conference on the eve of the Champions League match against Napoli that he could have been the manager of an Italian team today instead.

In a recent development, “In March, April, and May, there were contacts with an Italian team, but not with Napoli. I never spoke to the president of Napoli, I never spoke to anyone,” said the coach, a native of the province of Salerno.

Continuing in that press conference, the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss spoke rather intriguingly about the possibility of returning to work in Italy one day.

“You never know. I’m delighted to be here, because this is a great club, an organization that has had three coaches in the last 17 years. This reveals how differently we work, compared to my country. For Italian football, however, I say there’s no single solution,” he said.

“If we’re where we are, something needs to change. We need to be a little more courageous. Every time we miss a World Cup or a European Championship, people say everything needs to change, and then nothing ever changes.”.

Excluding Napoli – who last spring were already aware of Antonio Conte’s desire to leave – which club or clubs might have contacted Maresca shortly before the end of last season?

Maresca was one of the candidates Gerry Cardinale’s Milan considered, the report claims. The Rossoneri owner made it clear early in his search that he was looking for a coach capable of playing a dominant and attacking style of football.

Names like Andoni Iraola (who ended up at Liverpool) were also floated, but in the end Cardinale opted to go with Ruben Amorim, another coach with ties to Manchester given he had been sacked by United a few months prior.

The other avenue leads to Fiorentina, where Fabio Paratici was looking for a coach with different characteristics than Paolo Vanoli. La Viola’s sporting director had his eye on Maresca, but ultimately the courtship of City and being Guardiola’s successor was too appealing.

"[At half-time, the manager] wanted more aggression, more bodies," Fernandes told TNT Sports. "The first goal comes from that.

"We need points to get through. We need to focus on the next one. Now the moment is to get back to the Premier League. We need to stick together and fight for our lives.

Recent findings suggest that "Obviously, I think we started the game well. We gave a penalty away where Senne saved it. We gave one or two counters, but we were very good in recovery positions.

"They got the goal, but we were still in control of the game. We didn't have much people in the last third. Second half, we got the two goals. That was the moment we should push a bit more.

"Mistakes are part of football, and from that you get goals. Everyone has to take the blame for everything we do good and we do bad as well. We need to be together in the good and in the bad moments.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rasmus Hojlund told Manchester City fans ‘there is only one club in Manchester’ after scoring for Napoli in their Champions League clash on Tuesday night.

Hojlund scored the opening goal in the second half at the Etihad Stadiumbut City salvaged a 2-2 draw following Rayan Cherki’s equaliser in the 86th minute.

After scoring his first Champions League goal of the season with a brilliant low finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma, Hojlund celebrating in front of City’s supporters.

But before turning to the half way line, the Denmark international held up one finger and told the crowd: ‘There is only one club in Manchester’.

When asked about his celebration after the game, Hojlund mentioned: ‘Some good banter, you know.

In a recent development, ‘There’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and obviously I have a past in Manchester United. That’s my club. Nothing against City but United is my home.’.

Former Red, Rasmus Hojlund scoring at the Etihad tonight:“There’s only one club in Manchester” 🔴⚪️⚫️😍 pic.twitter.com/mS5eQsMWRA.

Hojlund joined Manchester United in a £72 million deal from Atalanta in 2023 and spent two seasons at Old Trafford before his loan move to Napoli.

The 23-year-old then completed a £38 million permanent move to Napoli this summer as the Serie A club had an obligation to sign him after qualifying for the Champions League.

During his two seasons at United, Hojlund scored 26 goals in 95 appearances.

Latest Update: Police arrest seven men after Man United's 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool at Anfield - with two suspected of illegal tragedy chanting

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.
  • The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 03:43 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:45 EST, 24 November 2026.

Merseyside Police reportedly arrested seven supporters at last weekend's clash between Manchester United and Liverpool, with two on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The bitter rivals met at Anfield for the first time in the Premier League season as Mauricio Pochettino kicked off his stint as Man United manager - under the most concerning circumstances.

But even before the visitors saw Leny Yoro sent off and four conceded without reply, this fixture has long been one of the most incendiary in the top flight.

Supporters arrested for suspected tragedy chanting are thought to be a 63-year-old man from Heywood, Greater Manchester, and a 57-year-old man from Wallasey, in Wirral, as per the Athletic.

Both clubs have waged independent battles against tragedy chanting, which sees fans taunt opponents by mocking major disasters, such as Hillsborough, the Heysel Stadium disaster, and the Munich air disaster.

Some tragedy chants are even aimed at the personal lives of players on the pitch, and in 2024, new guidance from the Crown Prosecution saw tragedy chanting upgraded to a criminal offence.

Seven people have been arrested following Man United's trip to face Liverpool at Anfield (police pictured breaking up a fight in the away end).

As well as tragedy chanting, a 47-year-old man from Swinton, Greater Manchester, was arrested on suspicion of possession of a class A drug.

Two men - a 49-year-old from Didsbury, South Manchester, and a 38-year-old from Denton, Greater Manchester - were arrested on suspicion of indecent and racialist chanting.

A further two, aged 30 and 23, were arrested during the final minutes of Sunday's clash as a skirmish broke out among the away supporters at Anfield.

But despite the enmity between the two teams, there were a greater number of arrests last month, when Man City visited Anfield for the first match in the wake of the revelation that the club had been found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them for breaching the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018.

That fixture saw 10 fans arrested, with five arrested on suspicion of tragedy chanting.

The match-up between the two sides became increasingly charged with the establishment of a rivalry at the top of the table under former managers Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola.

In 2018, the Man City bus was attacked with bottles, bricks and flares ahead of a Champions League meeting between the two sides, with future fixtures in Liverpool at times seeing the players' bus route amended to avoid throngs of home fans.

In March 2025, Merseyside police requested an unorthodox kick-off of 3.45pm for the match, rather than the customary Sunday start time of 4.30pm, in a bid to reduce problems between the two sets of fans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have successfully negotiated the option to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye once he turns 18.

Ndiaye, at the moment 16, trialled with Liverpool’s academy in the summer of 2025 and now has a clear pathway to Merseyside.

Per reports from The Athletic, the Reds have pipped a number of European rivals to get right of first refusal for his signing in January 2028.

English clubs cannot sign players from overseas until they have turned 18, which Ndiaye will do on Latest Year’s Eve in 2027.

Ndiaye currently plies his trade in his home nation with Diambars FC, whom he helped earn promotion to the Senegalese top flight last season.

Ndiaye is right now away at the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, picking up a goal and two assists in a 9-0 drubbing of Cuba earlier this week.

Senegal’s only other match at the tournament so far resulted in a 1-1 draw with Croatia. Liverpool fans hoping to get a glimpse of a future star, though, might be tempted to tune into their meeting with Tajikistan on Thursday, November 26.

Liverpool have made a habit of spotting talent at such tournaments. At last year’s U17 World Cup, their scouts brought home Senegal’s Mor Talla Ndiaye, Austria’s Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Belgium’s Lucca Brughmans.

It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will opt to sign Ndiaye in 2028, and what role he might play at the club if they do.

Ndiaye will hope to follow in the footsteps of one of Liverpool’s all-time greats, his countryman Sadio Mane, in making the move to the north-west.

By Darren Plant | 24 Nov 2026 22:55.

Unai Emery has suggested that Alejandro Garnacho is far away from a first start for Aston Villa.

On Tuesday night, the Premier League outfit succumbed to a 1-0 defeat at the hands of Galatasaray in the Champions League.

Not only are Villa now outsiders to finish in the top eight of the league phase, they have now gone six matches without a win in all competitions.

When quizzed on the prolonged wait for Garnacho to make his first Villa start, Emery has often been encouraging towards the Chelsea loanee.

However, when asked about his absence from the squad in Turkey, Emery hinted that the winger is not in his intends.

Emery named 11 substitutes - with two goalkeepers - for the Galatasaray game, one fewer than he was permitted.

Questioned over Garnacho not being involved, he told reporters: "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us.".

At his pre-match press conference, Emery stated that everyone was available, apart from Matty Cash, Matteo Ruggeri, Amadou Onana and the ineligible Brian Madjo.

Emery has been facing suggestions that Garnacho has been discarded from his intends in the same fashion as Liverpool loanee Harvey Elliott in 2025-26 since September.

He seemingly spoke sincerely when saying that Garnacho had made a positive impact during training and a friendly during the September international break.

Industry observers note that however, he remains with just 64 minutes across four substitute appearances since September 5. Although the appearances required for a permanent transfer from Chelsea has never been confirmed, the assumption is that it is 10 matches.

Garnacho is on seven outings, and there is now little to no realistic prospect of Emery choosing to activate a clause that would require Villa to pay approximately £43m for his signature.

As much as Villa's hierarchy and fans back Emery, questions need to be asked how two loanees who are known to have buy clauses in their respective agreements have been frozen out so promptly.

Villa have agreed separate deals worth a combined total of £78m. Elliott and Garnacho have made just three starts - all for Elliott - between them.

Haaland, meanwhile, endured another frustrating game as he failed to find the net and the Norway international registered just one shot on target against Napoli.

‘We managed to come back two times but we demand more, we have to do better, we have to find some ways to make us control the game more and perform in a better way,’ Haaland told beIN Sports after City’s draw at the Etihad Stadium.

According to recent reports, in a separate post-match interview, Haaland added: ‘Football is so easy and so difficult. When you win games everything is easy and you know what to do, and when you don’t win you start to question everything. The perfect thing to do is don’t think.

Mauricio Pochettino will not be able to call on Matheus Cunha as he chases his first win with Manchester United.

The Red Devils’ upcoming boss is facing just his second match in charge of the club as he looks to bounce back from the weekend’s chastening 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

He will return to the Champions League for the first time since leaving Paris Saint-Germain this evening, with a tricky tie away at Sporting on the docket.

However, in a selection blow, he will not be able to make use of one of his more threatening forwards, with Cunha left out of the Lisbon-bound travelling squad.

There was some positive news in the squad, though, as Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow came back into contention after injury layoffs, but the absence of Cunha is a serious setback for Pochettino as he looks to breathe life into his nascent United tenure.

Matheus Cunha was left out of the travelling squad for Manchester United’s meeting with Sporting as he is serving a red card suspension.

The Brazilian forward was dismissed in second-half injury time as United came from behind to beat Roma 3-2 last time out in the Champions League.

Having trailed by two goals to nil with just 17 minutes played, a second-half penalty from Bruno Fernandes and a quickfire brace from Cunha flipped the script.

Cunha, though, was shown two yellow cards in a chaotic finish.

The first came when he removed his shirt celebrating what proved to be the winning goal, and he picked up a second in the 91st minute for a needless, reckless late tackle on Leonardo Balerdi.

Cunha is only suspended for one match.

He will serve his suspension against Sporting tonight and be available again when United host RB Leipzig in two weeks’ time, on December 8.

Mauricio Pochettino has explained his decision to hand Joshua Zirkzee a first start of the season against Sporting in the Champions League.

The Argentine named just his second United team in Lisbon on Wednesday evening as he looked to bounce back from a damning 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on his managerial bow.

In Portugal, he made four changes from the side he named at Anfield, with Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui and Amad Diallo all coming into the side.

Perhaps his most notable call, though, saw striker Zirkzee chosen to lead the line, making his first start of the campaign.

The Dutchman has been bumped up the pecking order somewhat for this match, with fellow striker Benjamin Sesko out injured and deputy Matheus Cunha suspended.

Pochettino, though, stated he hopes Zirkzee can kick on as a more dependable option, given United’s thin ranks.

Asked to explain the selection, he told TNT Sports: “Cunha is suspended, of course, Sesko is injured. I think it is a great opportunity for Josh (Zirkzee) to show his quality.

“I think it is an key game to start to think that he can be a very important player for the team, and today is an opportunity for him.”.

Zirkzee was entirely peripheral under Michael Carrick and had looked to leave United in the summer transfer window. He was the subject of a loan bid from Everton on Deadline Day, but no move materialised.

Pochettino, though, seems optimistic he can bring Zirkzee in from the cold as United look to salvage their campaign, both domestically and abroad.

In a matchup featuring two of Ligue 1's biggest surprise stories at the moment, Brest will welcome Paris FC to Stade Francis-Le Ble on Friday.

A 1-0 win at Strasbourg on matchday 11 lifted the Brittany side to sixth in the Ligue 1 table, five points behind Paris, who are second after a convincing 4-0 triumph over Angers.

It appears as though Julien Lachuer has finally figured out the right buttons to push to help Brest find some consistency domestically.

This team entered November having dropped points in four of their last five league fixtures, but they will boast a 100% record this month should they triumph on Friday.

Brest can also win at least four domestic affairs in a row for the first time in a single league season since 2023-24 when they claimed six consecutive victories in this competition.

With a win on matchday 12, they would temporarily move into third place in Ligue 1 and that final Champions League spot above Lille on goal difference.

A team that gave up at least one goal in each of their first eight matches in this competition have not conceded in their last three such games.

After 11 matchdays, Les Pirates are third in Ligue 1 regarding expected goals but also rank third in big chances missed (23).

Liam Rosenior must be happy to be back in France, managing in a league where he has found tremendous success as a head coach.

The man who guided Strasbourg to a place in the Conference League has transformed Paris FC into title contenders, with his side just three points below Paris Saint-Germain heading into this match.

A victory by three or more goals on Friday would temporarily put them in first place and extend their winning run in this competition to four matches.

Right now, Paris FC are averaging 2.09 points per match in this competition, which is 0.80 more than a season ago, the biggest such increase among Ligue 1 clubs over that span.

They boast the lowest expected goals conceded in the league (10.2) and are one of three teams in the top flight that have not allowed a set-piece goal so far, with PSG and Lens being the others.

Paris FC can earn a third successive Ligue 1 triumph versus Brest on Friday, beating them 2-1 in their last visit to Stade Francis-Le Ble a season ago.

A calf strain may keep Brendan Chardonnet out of the Brest fold on Friday, while Kenny Lala is questionable with a knock and Kamory Doumbia is also doubtful with an ankle injury.

Noah Edjouma netted his third of the competition last week, while Egil Selvik stopped five shots to collect his third successive clean sheet in Ligue 1.

Meanwhile, for Paris FC, Nhoa Sangui may miss another match because of a hamstring problem which he has struggled to recover from.

Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all found the back of the net on matchday 11, with each strike coming in the second half.

Brest possible starting lineup:.

Selvik; Zogbe, Tousart, Lloris, Locko; Chotard, Magnetti; Edjouma, Nonge, Mboup; Ajorque.

Paris FC possible starting lineup:.

Trapp; Matondo, Chergui, Coppola, Otavio; Lopez, Lees-Melou; Kebbal, Zabi, Pagis; Koleosho.

While Brest are trending in the right direction, Paris FC have shown more consistency all season, and we believe their overall balance will see them collect maximum points once again.

Alexander Isak is closing in on a record held by Mohamed Salah with his latest Liverpool goal.

The Swedish striker did not take long to open the scoring as Liverpool faced Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Bradley Barcola won the ball high up the pitch to set the Reds on the attack and Dominik Szoboszlai teed Isak up to finish from close range.

It was a significant goal for Isak, who has now scored in six consecutive away matches for Liverpool.

It is a feat that very few men have bettered. According to the stat gurus at Opta, no Liverpool player has ever scored in more than seven consecutive away appearances.

Prior to the launch of the Premier League, Sam English, John Evans and John Aldridge all scored in seven consecutive away matches.

Salah called time on his Liverpool career at the end of last season, leaving with 257 goals and 123 assists across 442 appearances.

He now plies his trade in Turkey with Trabzonspor, where he has made a bright start to life, tallying 16 goal contributions in his first 17 appearances.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

It has been revealed that “I don’t know,” Sage mentioned when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old stated. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”.

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

“I cannot blame anybody because we didn’t do the job in a good way,” he remarked. “I’m responsible for this team, and when the team play as today, it’s not normal. It’s my fault. I understand them.

Sources indicate that “Another feeling is about shame because that’s my feeling after the game and from the beginning. It’s not normal to not respect the necessary of this kind of game.”.

Sage admitted that he will be assessing how Palace need to rethink their approach in the coming fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s trip to Besiktas in the Europa League.

It has been revealed that “The first work to do is on me,” he stated. “I’m responsible for what’s happened on the pitch, and I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing.

It has been revealed that “It’s maybe in the preparation, in the way we give them the motivation to start the game just before in the locker room in the warm-up. We have to analyse that because it’s not normal. And today it was really at the highest level we cannot expect, and that’s the moment to change the thing.”.

In a recent development, for all the scrutiny on his back three, Sage urged his entire side to take greater defensive responsibility, highlighting how the team were too passive in pressing Brighton. Palace have struggled to regain the solidity that long characterised the side since the departures of Marc Guéhi in January and Maxence Lacroix this summer.

“The way of defending is not only on the back three; it is for every player, and there are some things to do collectively, too,” Sage mentioned. “When we defend low we struggle a lot.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German mentioned: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”.

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Industry observers note that elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

You can also follow the latest updates from Manchester United’s crucial trip to Elland Road in our sister blog here.

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a big future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

According to recent reports, ‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that ‘If you play Estevao, you want him in the front three. Chances come in random ways, so he will get his chance again, and he has to do what he did the other day.

It has been revealed that ‘When he came on, I thought he was flying: not the weekend just gone, the weekend before that [against Sunderland. He came on and played really, really well.

‘So that’s him saying, “Look, I’m good enough to stay in your squad.” If he continuously does that, it becomes hard to ignore.’.

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

In a recent development, but when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’.

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on new signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their significant spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

Industry observers note that ‘I think at the very beginning he showed why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips mentioned when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a massive game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’.

Industry observers note that pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’.

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

Sources indicate that ‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

Sources indicate that ‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’.

Isak took his tally to 10 for the season with a double, his second a wonderful solo effort after shrugging off the attentions of giant centre-back Brandon Mechele to chip over the goalkeeper, while his fellow £100million-plus signing produced a goal equally exquisite.

The pair were the visitors’ best performers in a display which began well, lost its way in the middle, before finishing strongly with two expertly-taken strikes.

After defeat at Fenerbahce last time out it was imperative they responded against the Belgian champions, who had already beaten Inter Milan and PSV Eindhoven, and it was almost a textbook European away performance as they secured the points which lifted them into fifth.

Isak scored for the third successive game after 13 minutes and it was reward for pressuring goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

The Sweden international forced Sommer to misplace a pass which was picked up by Bradley Barcola.

He transferred the ball inside for Dominik Szoboszlai, captaining the team for the first time in the absence of Van Dijk, to cut back for his team-mate to poke home.

Isak was doing a good job of linking play, combining well with Wirtz especially, providing the first line of defence and was also a goal threat, with a snapshot wide from Barcola’s knockdown.

He looks more threatening and seems to have more understanding of Andoni Iraola’s gameplan by the day, but his new-found resilience will be tested to the full as it seems unthinkable he will not make his third start in a week against Everton.

The form of Wirtz, who scored his sixth goal in five matches for club and country, will also be a concern for the Toffees as the Germany international is brimming with confidence, highlighted by his goal.

When he received Rio Ngumoha’s pass 30 yards out he had only one thought in his mind: take a touch and shoot and he deceived Sommer by rattling a shot in off the goalkeeper’s right-hand post when it was easier to go the other side.

It was a classy finish to a game which had become a grind after the Reds failed to capitalise on their early advantage with Felix Lemarechal and Joaquin Seys having chances.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Alexander Isak believes Liverpool's "dangerous" attack is beginning to click after following up their win over Manchester United by beating Club Brugge in the Champions League.

Liverpool boosted their hopes of a top-eight finish with a 3-0 win at Jan Breydelstadion on Wednesday, with Isak netting either side of Florian Wirtz's superb 79th-minute finish.

Isak opened the scoring in the 13th minute, finishing after being teed up by Dominik Szoboszlai following Yann Sommer's sloppy pass that gifted Liverpool possession.

The Reds navigated a wave of Brugge pressure and put the game out of sight thanks to two late goals, with Wirtz scoring the first with a brilliant shot from just outside the penalty area.

Alisson then pumped a long ball forward for Isak to chase, with the Swede getting the better of Brandon Mechele before dinking the ball over Sommer and into the net.

Liverpool have now won consecutive matches by 3+ goals (4-0 v Man Utd and 3-0 v Brugge) for the first time since January (6-0 v Qarabag and 4-1 v Newcastle United).

Among all Premier League players, Isak has scored the joint-most away goals across all competitions this season (eight – level with Erling Haaland).

Bradley Barcola failed to register a goal involvement but looked dangerous, while Wirtz has now scored in three consecutive appearances for the first time as a Liverpool player, and for the first time overall at club level since September 2024 for Bayer Leverkusen (three).

"Perfect away win, I would say. The performance until we got the second one was never obvious which way it would go," Isak told TNT Sports.

"They put on a good game. We spoke about having to get the second goal. They were playing man-on-man, so I was against the defender the whole game.

"It's always difficult to say exactly where you are and how good you are, but I can say I'm in a good place and the team is in a good place, most importantly.

According to recent reports, "Hopefully, it gets better from here. The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations, and whoever comes in, we have a dangerous attack.".

But, more importantly, Liverpool were able to register their first clean sheet in the Champions League in 2026-27, with Alisson making five saves to keep Brugge at bay.

Sources indicate that in fact, Brugge were held goalless in the Champions League for the first time in 2026. In their first eight matches in the competition this year, they netted 22 goals at an average of 2.75 per game, but they could not find a way past Liverpool.

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

He is presently without a club.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

By Ben Sully | 25 Nov 2026 00:26, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 02:43.

Brentford are reportedly among three Premier League clubs interested in signing Lazio midfielder Kenneth Taylor.

The Bees splashed out around £41m to recruit midfielder Mamadou Sangare from Lens in the summer in a club-record transfer.

Sangare has featured in all 11 of Brentford's Premier League games, but he has not always been a guaranteed starter due to the competition from Vitaly Janelt and Yehor Yarmoliuk.

Mathias Jensen is also available to Brentford boss Keith Andrews, who currently has plenty of options at his disposal in central midfield.

However, Jensen is out of contract at the end of the season, and the uncertainty surrounding his future may be one of the factors behind Brentford's apparent interest in Taylor.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, the Bees are one of three Premier League clubs that are keeping tabs on the Dutchman's performances at Lazio.

Bournemouth and Newcastle United are also showing a keen interest as they scour the market for potential midfield recruits.

The Cherries are believed to view Taylor as a potential replacement for Alex Scott, who continues to draw interest from some of the Premier League's biggest clubs.

Meanwhile, Newcastle appear to be still open to bolstering a midfield that lost the services of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali at the end of last season, despite recruiting Nico Gonzalez and Aladji Bamba in the summer window.

Taylor has played regularly since joining Lazio from Ajax in January, contributing five goals and five assists in 34 competitive appearances.

In fact, he has registered two goals and three assists in 12 league matches this term, helping Gennaro Gattuso's side establish a two-point lead at the top of Serie A.

With Taylor under contract until June 2030, there is a belief his potential suitors will have to offer around €40m (£33m) to have any hope of prising him away from Lazio.

However, a January departure seems unlikely at this stage, with Gattuso keen to keep one of his key players for the club's title battle.

Brentford, Bournemouth and Newcastle will also have to be wary of rival interest from Juventus, who view him as the 'ideal' midfield target.
